issues.title: Incorrect signed response area and confidence interval
issues.quote: Inspecting individual probes also reveals that not all deviations are unprofitable: 3 of 40 small-cut probes under informative monitoring (across two seeds, max gain $0.003846$) and 1 of 40 under ablation (gain $0.000122$) yield positive conditional mean gains. Meanwhile, the signed rival-response area under informative monitoring averages $-3.7\times 10^{-6}$ price-period units (95\% CI: $[-1.1\times 10^{-5},\,3.2\times 10^{-6}]$), which is economically negligible. We also note that because Equation~\eqref{eq:latent} clamps latent means below $p^{\mathrm{N}}$, cuts from near-Nash prices can saturate the signal, limiting sensitivity to shock size (Appendix~B.2).
issues.analysis: The stated seed-level estimand yields -1.3628784654429182e-5 with CI [-2.52983136306284e-5,-3.4169651189586147e-6], corroborated by each impulse-path sum.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace estimate and interval; acknowledge the statistically resolved but tiny downward response.

issues.title: Prior imperfect-monitoring study misidentified
issues.quote: Classical repeated-game theory shows how firms can sustain supra-competitive prices under imperfect public monitoring when rival actions are hidden and only noisy public signals are observed \citep{green1984noncooperative, abreu1990toward, fudenberg1994folk}. In that literature, deviations are deterred when adverse public signals shift play into lower-value continuation regimes, balancing deviation detection against costly false alarms. In algorithmic pricing, \citet{calvano2020artificial} show that tabular Q-learning sustains supra-competitive prices under perfect price observation, and \citet{calvano2021algorithmic} extend tabular Q-learning to imperfect monitoring adapted from \citet{green1984noncooperative}, finding that discrete-price learners conditioned on short signal histories learn finite-duration ``price wars'' after adverse signals. Meanwhile, recent deep reinforcement learning studies such as \citet{deng2025exploring} compare tabular Q-learning, DQN, and PPO under perfect monitoring, focusing primarily on converged price levels.
issues.analysis: The checked primary author manuscript studies Cournot quantity actions and includes forced output interventions. The observational-only contrast is inaccurate.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct market/actions and credit the prior intervention diagnostic; see source locators in report.md.

issues.title: Unavailable implementation treated as reproducible archive
issues.quote: Use the archived source and build instructions. Supply the original \texttt{posterior\_draws.csv} and matching \texttt{posterior\_summary.csv}, verify the posterior hash, and run \texttt{require\_converged}. Preserve joint posterior rows; independent marginal sampling changes the training distribution.
issues.analysis: The full recursive repository and both original ZIPs contain outputs/manuscripts but no original trainer/native simulator/posterior/calibration data. Hash records cannot establish unavailable bytes or implementation semantics.
issues.suggested_fix: State the boundary and conditional reproduction requirements; distinguish file integrity from training/implementation validation.

issues.title: Null-spanning CI does not rule out unspecified large effects
issues.quote: Removing action information from the public channel therefore produces no statistically resolved reduction in converged prices or improvement in surplus. Because the confidence interval spans zero with ten seeds, this result shows the absence of a large channel effect rather than formal statistical equivalence. Effective feature rank (the exponential entropy of normalized eigenvalues of centered encoder features; Appendix~D) is slightly higher under ablation, reflecting the change in marginal report variance rather than a causal pricing mechanism.
issues.analysis: A CI spanning zero does not imply absence of a large effect without an explicit scale or equivalence margin.
issues.suggested_fix: Report unresolved effects of either sign and avoid absence/equivalence conclusions.

issues.title: Immediate-share strict inequality is too strong
issues.quote: Under informative monitoring, the average full gain is $-0.005192$ for the $0.1$ action cut and $-0.051322$ for the $0.3$ action cut, while the discounted continuation component $\Delta\pi^{\mathrm{cont}}$ averages only $-5\times 10^{-6}$ in both cases. Thus, over $99.9\%$ of the deviation loss is incurred immediately at the intervention step $t_0$ because baseline prices are already near $p^{\mathrm{N}}$. Under action-independent monitoring, immediate and full gains are identical to machine precision ($\Delta\pi^{\mathrm{cont}}=0$), confirming Proposition~\ref{prop:invariance}.
issues.analysis: The immediate/full ratios are 99.89827997% and 99.98971257%, so the first is below the stated bound.
issues.suggested_fix: Use an approximate percentage or report each cut separately.

issues.title: Early training attribution and steady decline unsupported
issues.quote: As shown in Figure~\ref{fig:elevation}, normalized price elevation starts near $0.43$ at the first checkpoint in both conditions ($0.4318$ informative vs.\ $0.4327$ action independent) as consequence of initial policy parameterization, and then declines steadily toward the Nash benchmark as learning progresses. By the final evaluation (Table~\ref{tab:final}), mean price elevation is $0.0151$ under informative monitoring and $0.0188$ under action-independent monitoring, with a paired difference of $0.0037$ (95\% bootstrap CI: $[-0.0241,\,0.0288]$).
issues.analysis: First checkpoint is after 12,288 interactions. Mean curves increase at 38/99 and 42/99 successive checkpoints. Initialization causation is untested.
issues.suggested_fix: Identify the checkpoint and describe an overall decline with fluctuations.

issues.title: Deng comparison misstates action and horizon scope
issues.analysis: The cited v1 uses a discrete PPO variant (15 prices) for comparison and describes a discounted MDP with finite training, rather than establishing an episodic terminal task.
issues.suggested_fix: Correct table scope; see arXiv v1 Sections 4.2–5.
